Clarification on the GPU shortage: It's a packaging capacity issue, not a wafer fabrication issue. Advanced substrate integration and HBM stacking are limiting shipments globally. #CoWoSCapacity

If you look at the Capex spending, TSMC is pouring billions specifically into expanding advanced packaging facilities in Taiwan, because raw EUV lithography is no longer the chokepoint for AI accelerators.

HBM3e yield rates and CoWoS packaging steps are the only metrics that matter for forecasting AI GPU deliveries this quarter. Silicon supply is fine.
It's fascinating how the industry narrative misses the mark. Everyone talks about nanometers and EUV machines, but the real constraint is the 2.5D packaging connecting the logic to the memory.
The complexity of placing 8 stacks of HBM precisely around a logic die on a silicon interposer with microscopic bumps is what's holding up the entire AI revolution.
Remember: CoWoS packaging and HBM availability = GPU supply. Wafer lithography is no longer the limiting factor. #CoWoSCapacity
Tracking back-end packaging equipment orders is the best leading indicator for future AI chip supply right now.

Careful reading the headlines—this isn't a rate cut or QE. The Fed is just tapering the balance-sheet runoff to ensure money-market plumbing remains stable while keeping rates restrictive. 📉💼 #FedBalanceSheet

This is a purely mechanical liquidity adjustment. Slowing QT to $25B/month allows the Fed to cautiously find the 'ample reserves' threshold without abruptly shocking the overnight funding markets. Rate policy remains entirely unchanged.

Powell made it clear in the presser: slowing the runoff cap is independent of the interest rate path. It's solely to ensure smooth functioning of the repo and reserve markets.

posts.text: Important clarification by the Open Source Initiative: releasing just the compiled model weights with restrictive acceptable-use clauses is NOT 'Open Source'. True open-source AI requires releasing the pre-training datasets and data-filtering code! 📜🔍 #OSIAIDefinition

This debate is critical. 'Open-weight' is great for inference, but if you don't have the training data and the recipe, you cannot fully study, modify, or reproduce the model. Calling a black-box matrix of weights 'open source' dilutes the definition established in the 1990s.
We need strict technical distinction! An open-weight release is a black box if the training corpus is hidden. Fully reproducible open-source AI must include the data! 🧠⚖️ #OSIAIDefinition

The OSI standard draft explicitly states that for an AI system to be open source, a skilled person must be able to recreate it. You can't do that without the datasets and the filtering pipelines.

It's a crucial legal and technical distinction. If a model has a license restricting commercial use or specific applications, it fails the Open Source Definition immediately, even if the weights are public.
Open-weights ≠ Open Source. The training data IS the source code! 🧠🔍 #OSIAIDefinition

I appreciate companies dropping weights, but they need to be honest. If the recipe is a trade secret, the AI is not open source.

Identity and access management is failing us. Social engineering beat billion-dollar firewalls again! 😰🚨 #CloudBreachVector
If your helpdesk can bypass MFA without hardware key verification, your company is already compromised. 😡💻
We mandate FIDO2 hardware keys for all infrastructure access now. You can't phish a YubiKey, and you can't replay a stolen session token if it's cryptographically bound to the device.

Social engineering is the deadliest threat vector today. Not zero-days, just stolen session cookies! 😰🔐 #CloudBreachVector
Humans are the weakest link in the cloud security chain! Frustrating! 😡🚨
It's known as 'MFA fatigue' or 'prompt bombing'. They spam the user's phone with 50 approval requests at 3 AM until the user gets annoyed and clicks 'Accept'.
Helpdesks need to implement strict visual verification and manager sign-off for any MFA resets. The days of trusting a voice over the phone are over.
Identity is the perimeter! Secure your session tokens! 😰💻 #CloudBreachVector
No code exploits, just clever phishing. We need better training! 😡🔐
Session hijacking completely bypasses all the zero-trust network architecture marketing hype if the token itself is trusted implicitly.
The attackers understand our organizational charts and internal IT processes better than we do.

We need continuous authentication that monitors behavior, not just a one-time token check at login.

posts.text: URGENT: This is not a drill! An unauthorized Autonomous System just executed a massive BGP prefix hijack, redirecting 440 financial institution IPv4 prefixes through an unverified transit provider in Eastern Europe! They held the route for 72 minutes before RPKI ROA filtering finally kicked in. 🚨😨 #BGPRoutingLeak

Network architect here. The implications of this BGP hijack are terrifying. For 72 minutes, highly sensitive banking traffic was routed through a hostile AS. Even with HTTPS, the risk of TLS interception or metadata analysis is immense. The fact that several Tier-1 ISPs accepted the bogus route announcements shows how incomplete RPKI adoption still is.

The core routing protocol of the internet is fundamentally broken by trust! A 72-minute BGP hijack of banking traffic is a catastrophic security failure! Deeply anxious about what data they captured! 😰🌐 #BGPRoutingLeak

We saw the route changes propagate in our BGP looking glass. The malicious AS announced a more specific /24 route, overriding the legitimate /22 block owned by the banks. Standard longest-prefix-match routing meant global traffic blindly followed the hijack. Absolute nightmare.
Every bank needs to check their certificate transparency logs NOW! If they attempted TLS interception during that 72-minute BGP hijack, we have a massive breach! 🚨📉 #BGPRoutingLeak
RPKI ROA validation saved us from this being permanent, but 72 minutes is more than enough time to siphon gigabytes of encrypted payloads for future quantum decryption. Terrifying! 😨🔐 #BGPRoutingLeak

This highlights the critical vulnerability in inter-domain routing. If your upstream transit provider doesn't enforce strict Route Origin Validation (ROV), your traffic is at the mercy of any rogue AS operator with a BGP session.

The malicious AS prepended their AS path to make it look legitimate, bypassing basic route filters. The coordination required to hijack 440 specific financial prefixes implies state-sponsored level targeting. Very worried.
BGP hijacks of financial networks! The internet backbone is dangerously fragile! 😰🌐 #BGPRoutingLeak
Frantically reviewing packet captures from the 72-minute window. This BGP leak is a massive security incident! 🚨📉
We need global mandates for RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure). Relying on IRR databases that haven't been updated in a decade is why these hijacks keep succeeding.
The downstream effects on API latency were the first indicator. The traffic tromboning to Eastern Europe and back added 150ms to every transaction before the routes were withdrawn.
BGP security is a joke until every Tier-1 enforces strict ROA! Anxious for the fallout! 😨🔐 #BGPRoutingLeak
72 minutes of banking traffic diverted! The ultimate man-in-the-middle attack! 🚨🌐
I'm terrified of what a sophisticated actor could do with that much intercepted traffic, even if it's encrypted. Traffic analysis alone reveals trading patterns.
The AS that leaked the routes claims it was a 'configuration error', but you don't accidentally type in 440 specific financial /24 blocks. This was intentional.
The internet runs on trust, and that trust was just exploited massively! 😰 #BGPRoutingLeak
Check your route announcements constantly! This is terrifying! 🚨📉
Our NOC lit up like a Christmas tree when the route paths shifted. We dropped our BGP sessions with the affected transit provider immediately.
Until BGPsec is widely adopted to cryptographically verify the entire AS path, not just the origin, we remain vulnerable to path manipulation.
